On TypeScript the NAPI-backed (Node/Bun) runtime signs and surfaces the signature on Checkpoint.signature via bindings/typescript/src/internal/native.ts. Checkpoint is a flat always-signed interface matching the Python/Swift/Kotlin SDKs; the runtime populates the 64-byte (128-hex-char) Ed25519 signature. There is no `signed` discriminant. The byte layout of the signing payload is identical across all bridges (compute_checkpoint_canonical_hash).

operations.name: scp_new
operations.notes: SCP(storage) constructor — the only entry point into the SDK. Storage selection is MANDATORY and fail-closed (spec §17.6): there is no zero-argument constructor and no default backend. Python scp_sdk.SCP(storage={...}), TypeScript new SCP({ storage: {...} }), Kotlin SCP(storage), Swift SCP(storage:) / SCP.withStorage(_:). The two selections are {type: in_memory} (development) and {type: sqlite, ...} (production). Statically-typed bridges (UniFFI typed StorageConfig, required Swift/Kotlin/TS argument) reject a missing selection at compile time; dynamically-typed bridges (PyO3 dict, NAPI JSON string) reject it at runtime with SCP-STORAGE-8000. Each constructor allocates a fresh BridgeInstance (PyBridgeInstance / NapiBridgeInstance / UniffiBridgeInstance) with its own registries, ContextManager, transport manager, and monotonic instance_id. Multiple instances in one process are supported — identities and relay connections do not leak across them. See ADR-048 §Decision 1 and spec §17.6. The pre-PR-4 `SCP.default()` accessor and underlying `DEFAULT_BRIDGE_INSTANCE` OnceLock were DELETED in PR 4 (re-scoped 2026-04-19): no deprecation window, no sunset scaffold.

operations.name: scp_with_storage_in_memory
operations.notes: SCP.withStorage({type: "in_memory"}) — in-memory storage variant. Default for tests and ephemeral workflows. Symmetric with with_storage_sqlite below. PyO3 SCP(storage={"type": "in_memory"}), NAPI SCP.withStorage({type: "in_memory"}), Swift SCP.withStorage(.inMemory), Kotlin SCP.withStorage(StorageConfig.InMemory).

operations.name: scp_instance_id
operations.notes: Monotonic u64 instance identifier assigned at SCP() construction. Exposed as a read-only property ON THE SCP CLASS ONLY. Every handle type (ContextHandle, Identity, UcanToken, MessageReceiver, ...) carries its owning SCP's instance_id as a Rust-internal field — this per-handle id is NOT host-visible (no per-handle instanceId getter/export on any bridge; see ADR-048 §Per-handle host-visible instanceId is NOT exposed). Every handle-accepting FFI function runs a runtime affinity check (SCP-PERM-3030 on mismatch) enforced by scripts/check-handle-affinity.sh. Python scp.instance_id, TypeScript scp.instanceId, Kotlin scp.instanceId, Swift scp.instanceId.

operations.name: shutdown_timeout
operations.notes: SCP.shutdown(timeout) — bounded graceful shutdown replacing the Phase 4 PR 1 terminal infallible shutdown. Propagates a tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken into every long-running task, waits on a JoinSet up to the timeout, and forcibly cancels anything still running at the deadline. Async across all bridges: PyO3 returns a coroutine, NAPI returns Promise<void>, UniFFI generates Kotlin suspend fun / Swift async throws. Timeout is carried as u64 milliseconds across all three bridges (NAPI was widened from u32 in #1692). Each SDK wrapper clamps to its bridge's maximum at the boundary. See ADR-048 §Decision 5 and §Notes/Shutdown-timeout integer width across FFI bridges.

operations.name: suspend
operations.notes: Disconnects transport and marks BridgeInstance as suspended for mobile/desktop backgrounding. All three FFI bridges (PyO3 scp_suspend, NAPI scpSuspend, UniFFI scpSuspend) call BridgeInstance::suspend. Phase 4 PR 4 (#1549) deleted the free-function SDK wrappers; SCP.suspend() is now the only entry point in every SDK: Python scp.suspend(), TypeScript scp.suspend(), Kotlin scp.suspend(), Swift scp.suspend().

operations.name: resume
operations.notes: ASYNC as of Phase 4 PR 3 (#1678, 2026-04-18) — BREAKING CHANGE. BridgeInstanceCore::resume is async fn; per-bridge overrides reconnect every pending relay URL and restore persisted contexts before returning. Reconnect failures surface as LifecycleError::ReconnectFailed { url, reason }. All three FFI bridges expose the async path: PyO3 releases the GIL and block_ons, NAPI returns a Promise, UniFFI generates Kotlin suspend fun / Swift async throws. Phase 4 PR 4 (#1549) deleted the free-function SDK wrappers; SCP.resume() is now the only entry point in every SDK: Python async def resume(), TypeScript scp.resume(): Promise<void>, Kotlin scp.resume() (suspend fun), Swift func resume() async throws.

operations.name: with_storage_sqlite
operations.notes: SCP.withStorage(Sqlite { path, key }) exposes the SQLCipher-backed SqliteStorage across all three bridges (#1491, #1260; Phase 4 PR 3, 2026-04-18). The StorageConfig::Sqlite key field is a SqliteKeyMaterial sum type accepting EITHER raw key material (Raw, 32-byte key validated at the FFI boundary) OR a passphrase (Passphrase, SQLCipher key derived via Argon2id with a persisted per-database salt sidecar). For sqlite, exactly ONE of key/passphrase must be supplied — both or neither is a ValidationError; both forms are wrapped in Zeroizing. PyO3 accepts Python bytes (key) or a str (passphrase); NAPI accepts a hex string OR Uint8Array (key) or a string (passphrase); UniFFI generates Swift StorageConfig.sqlite(path:key:) / SqliteKeyMaterial.raw|.passphrase and the Kotlin equivalents via #[derive(uniffi::Enum)]. SDK convenience constructors: Swift SCP.withStorage(sqliteDir:key:)/passphrase variant, Kotlin SCP.withSqlite(dir, key)/passphrase variant, Python SCP.with_storage({...}), TypeScript SCP.withStorage({...}). The Supervisor's mls_storage view, context-snapshot persistence, and event log all share a single rusqlite::Connection via the one Arc<SqliteStorage>.

operations.name: add_relay_url
operations.notes: CoreFields::relay_url (Mutex<Option<String>>) replaced with relay_urls (Mutex<HashSet<String>>) in Phase 4 PR 3 (#1678, 2026-04-18). New accessors add_relay_url / remove_relay_url / pending_relay_urls; each per-bridge resume() iterates the HashSet and reconnects each URL. First reconnect failure surfaces as LifecycleError::ReconnectFailed { url, reason }; successfully-connected URLs remain in the pending set for retry.

coverage_exemptions.kotlin: Present in the UniFFI bridge as `addRelay` (generated from `crates/scp-ffi/uniffi/src/bridge.rs` — the `add_relay_url` export in TransportManager). The generated Kotlin file (`works.limn.scp.internal.uniffi.scp.TransportManager.addRelay`) is not git-tracked; verify via `cargo build -p scp-ffi-uniffi`. The generated file's backtick-quoted, @Throws-annotated override methods are not surfaced as clean function_declaration nodes by the tree-sitter-kotlin grammar the coverage extractor uses, so the symbol cannot be statically matched.

call_invariants.description: The runtime `enforce_send_economy` helper must delegate to the unified `enforce_economy` function (economy.rs). Skipping delegation would let `ContextManager::send_message` bypass budget/velocity/UCAN checks for paid contexts.

`lifecycle_helpers::import_context` must call `validate_export_for_import` before touching event log or crypto state. Skipping validation lets a malformed or malicious snapshot install a broken MLS group or corrupt the Merkle chain.

Every bridge's `identity_create` entrypoint must call `ensure_did_resolver_initialized_on` before returning. The resolver is a per-bridge-instance slot used by UCAN validation (#311, ADR-048 renamed the helper from `ensure_did_resolver_initialized` to the `_on` suffix convention for per-instance helpers in Phase 4 PR 5); skipping initialization degrades UCAN verification to string-only lookups.
